title: Helping General and Specialty Contractors get more done: What’s new at Groundbreak 2026
summary: Fixing the basics you’ve asked for, and building the things you’d never think to ask for
body_markdown:
At Groundbreak this year, I shared a piece of feedback one of you gave me that I haven’t been able to shake: “Geoff, AI is great, but can you just fix Procore so I can bulk edit submittal workflows? Please nail the basics.”


Spot on. We don’t earn the right to talk about things like our[Digital Coworker](https://www.procore.com/press/procore-introduces-digital-coworker-packages-expands-ai-agent-library-and-previews-skills-to-help-construction-teams-put-ai-to-work) AI agents until we’ve nailed the basics. (And yes, bulk editing of submittal workflows is live.)


So that’s where we spent a lot of this year. Our teams got out on jobsites and sat with you to see exactly where Procore is great and where it’s rough, in gory detail. We’ve shipped over five hundred improvements this year to the parts of Procore your teams use every day, and there’s a lot more coming.


At[Groundbreak 2026](https://www.procore.com/blog/groundbreak-2026-putting-the-future-of-construction-to-work) , I walked through what’s next for general contractors and specialty contractors. A lot of it is the basics that you and your teams rely on to get the job done every single day. And a lot of it is innovative stuff, like AI that actually does work for you. All of it comes from listening to you and building what you actually need.


Here’s what we announced.


### **Fewer Surprises When the Crew Shows Up**


*For general contractors and specialty contractors*


Think about a mechanical contractor waiting on equipment for a hospital job. The submittal is approved. Then the delivery date slips, and nobody finds out until the crew shows up to install it. Now you’re paying for idle labor by the hour, and the schedule is at risk.


Most of the time, that information existed somewhere. It was just stuck in an email chain, a spreadsheet, or another company’s system. Last year I said our goal with Procore Connect was that you’d never again have to ask “whose Procore account are we using?” We got a lot closer this year.


Here’s what we’re doing to get everyone working from the same information and catch a slip while there’s still time to adjust:


-


**Procore Scheduling Links to Submittals and Procurement:** In closed beta, it enables teams to link schedule activities to the submittals and, with[Procurement Log](https://www.procore.com/library/construction-procurement-log-template) , the materials they depend on, so a slip can show up on the activity while there’s still time to adjust.


-


**Document Management:** In closed beta in the US, helps teams manage design packages and project documents in one place, track issues across revisions, and publish the latest approved version to the field. That helps crews build from the current set.


-


**Procore Connect Enhancements:**


-


**RFI Collaboration:** In open beta, allows general contractors and specialty contractors to collaborate on RFIs from their own Procore accounts, with updates shared automatically. This helps reduce duplicate data entry, back-and-forth emails, and the risk of working from outdated information.


-


**Connected Daily Manpower Log:** In closed beta, automatically shares crew and labor information between connected Procore accounts in real time, helping teams maintain accurate records without entering the same information twice.


-


**My Open Items Workspace:** Available now, brings all tasks assigned to you across projects and partner accounts into one list, making it easier to see what needs your attention without switching between accounts.


-


**Model Manager:** In open beta, lets teams pin or link issues and items to the 3D model and see their status. That gives the field and office the same view of what’s open, what’s approved, and where it is before the crew shows up.


-


**Locations:** Available now, brings the issues and items tied to a floor, zone, or segment into one view. Crews can check what’s still open in their area before they mobilize, or scan a location’s QR code on site to see it.


### **See What’s Coming, Not Just What Happened**


*For general contractors*


When I sit with execs, the questions sound like this: Which jobs are trending late? Where am I going to fade margin next quarter? Where’s my risk sitting right now? And on the budget, it’s always the same question: what changed since last month, and why?


You’ve got the data to answer all of that. It’s in Procore. The problem is it doesn’t do anything until somebody acts on it. Hubs and[Insights](https://www.procore.com/insights) are how we’re closing that gap, so you see problems sooner and step in before they grow.


I was walking a COO through Procore recently. Twenty minutes in, he was polite but half on his phone. Then we put one screen up: this month’s budget next to last month’s, every line that moved, and why. He put the phone down, walked up to the screen, and asked when he could get a demo. That’s the kind of reaction we’re building for.


-


**Safety Hub and Portfolio Hub:** Available now, Hubs are built around the questions leaders ask most, so the answers they used to chase are in one place.[Safety Hub](https://www.procore.com/blog/introducing-safety-hub-now-in-open-beta) covers safety risk across projects, and Portfolio Hub covers cost, submittals, and safety across the business. Examples include overdue observations and jobs trending over on cost, which helps leaders step in sooner.


-


**Procore Insights:** Available now for individual projects and across the portfolio, helps teams spot risk sooner by connecting the dots in project data and pointing to where they should look. That gives teams more time to act before an issue reaches the budget or the schedule. Quality Issue Predictions is one example, highlighting issues a job may run into based on a company’s own history plus industry and regional patterns.


-


**Procurement Log:** In closed beta, helps project teams tie every material’s order and delivery status to the submittals and schedule that drives it, helping to spot delivery risk early and keep the job on track, without living in a spreadsheet.


-


**Company Managed Periods with Project Status Snapshots:** In open beta, enables teams to capture a consistent picture of project health and compare performance over time. This makes it easier to track changing costs, spot budget trends, and understand what’s changed from one month to the next by project and across the portfolio.


-


**Company-Level Direct Costs:** Releasing in the coming weeks, will allow teams to record and approve project expenses that aren’t tied to a purchase order or subcontract. Planned Procore Pay capabilities will also make it possible to pay these invoices directly through Procore.


-


**Procore Pay Updates:** Available now, helps general contractors manage paperwork and payments more efficiently. Teams can see which invoices are ready for payment, automatically remind specialty contractors about missing compliance paperwork, track payments made outside Procore, and pay approved invoices, keeping payment information in one place while also updating critical ERP systems for a reliable source of truth.


-


**Bidding and Estimating Integration:** Releasing in the coming weeks, connects the Estimating and Bidding tools so teams can create bid packages directly from estimate line items, send invitations to subcontractors, and pull awarded bid values back into the estimate, all without leaving Procore or re-entering data manually.


### **Capture the Work & Protect Your Margins**


*For specialty contractors and general contractors doing their own construction work*


Every dollar of self-perform work starts as a unit quantity times a rate. And for a lot of you, those rates live in spreadsheets, printed union agreements, and somebody’s memory.


So when a crew spends an extra day on work outside the original scope and nobody writes it down as it happens, the office is left piecing together labor, equipment, and materials after the fact. That’s work you did and might not get paid for.


When margins are this tight, every hour counts. We’ve put a lot into project controls this year so the work gets captured in the field as it happens and tied straight to cost. And honestly, the reaction has been one of my favorite parts of the year. One of the biggest mechanical contractors in the Northwest sent us a note about Rate Tables: “Rate tables went right to my soul. Rates have been an unsolvable mystery for us forever.” Right to the soul. For rate tables! That’s what makes my job fun.


-


**Time & Materials to Change Orders:** In development, when a crew performs extra work, the foreman can document the labor, equipment, and materials used. With the Rates open beta, that information can move into a Change Event in Procore, reducing duplicate entry and helping make sure costs tied to approved extra work don’t get missed when it’s time to bill.


-


**AI-Assisted Timesheet Capture:** Entering closed beta in Q4, this capability will help crews take a photo of a paper timesheet and automatically extract the hours into Procore Timesheets for review, eliminating the need to enter them by hand.


-


**Rate Tables:** Available now, Rate Tables let specialty contractors define labor and equipment rates once and apply them across timesheets, time-and-materials tickets, and change orders. That means less time looking up rates and fewer opportunities for pricing mistakes.


-


**Production Tracking:** In development, Production Tracking will help teams measure progress based on work completed, not just hours spent. For example, a mechanical contractor could track the stages of a piping installation, from welding to testing and insulation, to get a clearer picture of what’s finished and what’s left.


-


**Resource Planning with SmartBench:** Available now,[SmartBench](https://www.procore.com/resource-planning) uses AI to recommend workers for upcoming jobs based on skills, availability, and location. New Gantt views are also planned to help teams visualize crew assignments over time.


-


**Simplified Invoicing:** In open beta, Simplified Invoicing gives teams a streamlined alternative to the Construction Progress Invoicing format for Commitments. Select it on a commitment before any invoices are created to bill in a format that fits how you work, with all of Procore's financial controls still in place.


-


**Worksheet Columns:** In open beta, provides a single view that pulls production quantities from every source that feeds the budget, including the original budget, budget changes, prime contract change orders, and change events, into one column, with units of measure shown right in the cell.


-


**Percent-Based Advanced Forecasting:** In open beta, enables teams to enter monthly forecast values as a percentage of committed value instead of calculating dollar amounts by hand. Each forecast view can hold its own spread, so a billing forecast and a revenue forecast on the same budget line don’t overwrite each other.


### **Spend Less Time Searching and More Time Building**


*For general contractors and specialty contractors*


Think about a foreman in the middle of an install when a question comes up about a drawing detail. The answer is in Procore somewhere. Finding it means stopping work, digging through files, or calling someone back at the office.


Those interruptions add up. And this is where I get to talk about the fun part. Where we’re heading with[Procore AI](https://www.procore.com/ai) is technology that doesn’t just help you get work done, but actually does work for you. It starts with making it easy for crews to get answers and knock out routine tasks without walking away from the work in front of them.


-


**Procore AI Go:** In open beta, a voice-first mobile app that lets crews ask questions about drawings, specifications, RFIs, and submittals and receive spoken answers based on their project information in Procore. A foreman can ask a question into their phone and get an answer without stopping to search through documents.


-


**Procore AI Agents:** Available now,[Procore AI agents](https://www.procore.com/ai/agents) help teams handle repetitive tasks, such as reviewing submittals and identifying missing or inconsistent information. Instead of starting every review from scratch, construction professionals can focus on the items that need their expertise.


-


**Control Tower:** Available now, Control Tower helps companies oversee AI usage across their projects. General contractors and specialty contractors can monitor agent activity and credit consumption from one place, helping them manage usage and costs.


-


**AI Built for Construction:** Procore AI is designed to understand how construction information connects across drawings, specifications, RFIs, and submittals. This helps teams find more relevant answers and identify potential inconsistencies before they affect work in the field.


-


**Agent Marketplace:** Available now, the Agent Marketplace extends Procore AI with agents from trusted technology partners. For example, a general contractor can use a partner agent to help find rental equipment for an upcoming job without switching between systems.


### **Building What’s Next, Together**


The way we build hasn’t changed in more than twenty years: we listen to you, we watch how your teams use the product, and we build what you actually need. That’s our DNA.


For general contractors, that means a clearer view and more control across every project. For specialty contractors, it means better ways to manage crews, track progress, and protect margin. For everyone, it means fixing the basics you’ve asked for and building the things you’d never think to ask for.


The technology is going to keep changing, and fast. Procore was there when construction moved to the cloud and when it moved onto your phone. We’re here for AI, and we’ll be here for whatever comes next. What you build will outlast all of it. Our job is to keep listening, keep partnering with you, and keep delivering, so you can build it well.


> Groundbreak 2026 is officially a wrap, but what we’re building together is just getting started. Join us in Anaheim, California, for Groundbreak 2027 as we continue shaping the future of construction together.
